chapter: Back to the horn: house sessions
title: Bill Walde's family and a benefit at the Plum Plan
summary: He names the Walde brothers and recalls a benefit dance at the low tin-roofed Plum Plan.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And his brothers, too. Henry, too. And August. You know August? Yeah, sure.

I know them all. Henry used to come out there to the sessions. What are you talking about? A nice, a guy who plays relaxed music. It's him. You ever hear him play? Oh, he plays a nice kid, too. I played a benefit dance at Plum Plan one night. And it's a wonderful place to play. Paul's a good place. I was a good place to play. I was a good place to play. And it's a wonderful place to play, Paul. It's got a low tin roof. Man, that music really bounces back at you. And we had my little fella, Alvin, on piano. Henry on guitar. Billy's brother on bass. And myself and Raymond. Oh, you're talking about. Play some music. Man, it really sounded nice. Why do they call it the Plum Plan? I don't know, Dick. You talk about a place used to have some knockout and drag out fights. Ain't that?
I used to go hear Buck Band a little bit. Yeah. That was fun. I know, Paul.
dear playing clarinet and I can't recall the piano man. And I can't recall the bass man.
